definition: Isabelle Guyon (French pronunciation: [izabɛl ɡɥijɔ̃]; born August 15, 1961) is a French-born researcher in machine learning known for her work on support-vector machines, artificial neural networks and bioinformatics.
details: She is a Chair Professor at the University of Paris-Saclay. Guyon serves as the Director of Research at Google DeepMind since October 2022. She is considered to be a pioneer in the field, with her contribution to the support-vector machines with Vladimir Vapnik and Bernhard Boser.

explainer.lead: Isabelle Guyon is a French-born researcher in machine learning (born 1961). Her work spans informatics, bioinformatics, artificial neural network and machine learning.

contributions.name: She founded ChaLearn in 2011, a non-profit organization aimed at creating machine learning challenges open to everyone.
She is also a co-inventor of the siamese neural networks, a neural network architecture used to learn similarities, with applications to signature, face or object recognition.

timeline.what: Guyon defended her thesis in 1988 and was hired the year after at AT&T Bell Laboratories, first as a post-doc, then as a group leader.
In 1996, Guyon left Bell Labs and raised her children at Berkeley, California.
Since 2003, Guyon has organized many challenges in data science, in order to stimulate research in this field.
She was Program Chair of NeurIPS 2016 and became General Chair of NeurIPS in 2017.
Receives the Knight of the Legion of Honour
